text.p: These are the major headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- School-funding change urged: David Crombie recommends overhaul that would benefit Catholic, rural students.
- Military examines reports of beating: Female officer focus of probe.
- Train in India bombed: People suspect local guerrillas.
- Officer aids children shivering in bus shelter at night: Scruffy off-duty appearance draws wary response from pair.
- Canadian farming grows into big business: Agriculture has entered a high-tech era in which brains, not brawn, signal a successful enterprise.
- Reformed British soccer fit for the Queen.
- TSE trading sets new mark: Value of $300.5-billion blasts past last year's total by nearly $100-billion.
- Low rates expected to bear fruit in 1997: Economists predict spending spurge, robust dollar as lending costs plummet.
- Calgary office market rebounds from glut: TrizecHahn, Oxford line up tenants.
- Softwood deal casts shadow over market.
- Unique software thinks like a human.
